Talking knocked out the USB cable

While you transmitted on this channel the phone's USB port reset: the phone stopped charging and, with Android Auto on a cable, the car disconnected until you stopped talking. It does not matter which Talk button you used.

The radio's own signal gets into the USB cable. Whether it does depends on the frequency, not on where the antenna is: in one car a 2 m repeater transmitting on 144.770 MHz at high power did it every time, while 146.370 MHz did not.

What helps:
• a snap-on ferrite choke on the cable, close to the phone
• a shorter, better-shielded cable
• Low power for this channel (Channels → edit the channel)
• wireless Android Auto, if the car has it

Android Auto connected but never loaded the radio on this connection (normally it does within a few seconds), so SignalDeck was missing from the car\'s app list and its card opened the app on the phone. Unknown sources was on, so this is Android Auto\'s own hiccup, seen once after it had just started up. Unplug the USB cable and plug it in again: on the new connection it loads the radio.
Android Auto is hiding the radio

Android Auto only trusts apps installed from the Play Store. For this app it plays the sound and the steering-wheel buttons work, but SignalDeck is missing from the car\'s app list and tapping its card opens the app on the phone.\n\n%1$s

Another source started playing in the car (music, an audio app, the car\'s own radio, or a call), so Android Auto gave it the speakers and the radio\'s sound paused. The radio keeps receiving, recording and decoding meanwhile. Press play on the radio\'s card or media screen to get the speakers back. Just before a disconnection this line is normal: Android Auto takes the sound away as it closes.
The phone connected to the car. In brackets: what the car lists for the radio, the media app (SignalDeck) or the full-screen Radio controls (Device → Full-screen Radio controls in the car).

The connection to the car ended: the car was switched off, the cable was unplugged, or the link dropped. Look at Around this time below: if you were transmitting just before (a Voice TX line), the transmission probably disturbed the USB cable, and an alert says so when the app noticed.
Android Auto opened the radio\'s screen in the car (the media app\'s channel list, or Radio controls).

After you transmitted on this repeater channel, the app listened for the repeater\'s answer (its signal coming back after you let go) and heard none. The coverage map marks this spot as not reaching the repeater. Either the repeater did not hear you, or you could not hear it.
After you transmitted, the repeater\'s signal came back: this spot reaches it. The level is the repeater\'s tail as heard here, and the coverage map records it.

Coverage logging records the signal and your key-ups with GPS for the coverage maps (Map → Coverage). With Device → Log coverage in the car on, it starts when Android Auto connects and stops when it disconnects.

NOAA weather channels (162.400 to 162.550 MHz) marine VHF channels (156.000 to 157.450 MHz) and the AAR railroad channels (159.810 to 161.565 MHz) are receive-only. The radio does not transmit there, whatever button is pressed.
This radio\'s firmware ends every transmission after 30 seconds, so the app refuses audio longer than about 28.5 seconds (for example a long recording or an SSTV mode that needs more time).
The radio refused to transmit because the channel was busy: another station was on it, or on DMR the repeater\'s time slot was in use. Wait for it to clear and try again.

The repeater sent its callsign in Morse, as repeaters must every few minutes while in use, and the app decoded it. It matches the callsign in this channel\'s name, so you are hearing the repeater you programmed (not another one on the same frequency). The tone and speed are shown in brackets.

Morse code was heard on this channel and decoded: usually a repeater\'s identification, or a station sending its callsign. Callsigns in it are added to the Logbook as heard. PKT \u2192 Settings \u2192 Morse decoder turns it off.
Live captions heard one of your keywords in received speech. Keywords are set on the intercom: long-press TXT → Keywords.
The transmission was refused before keying. Packet radio (APRS, DTMF, SSTV) needs an analog FM channel: AFSK tones cannot go out over DMR. Tune an FM channel and try again.
Nothing heard on this channel yet.

On the phone open Android Auto\'s settings, scroll to the bottom and tap Version ten times (confirm the prompt) to unlock the developer settings. Then tap the ⋮ menu at the top right, choose Developer settings and turn on Unknown sources. Then disconnect and reconnect the car: SignalDeck appears on the car\'s app list and its card opens the car\'s media screen.
